compareCandidate.label: Prime vs. composite
compareCandidate.description: A prime has exactly two factors (1 and itself). A composite has more — it can be broken into smaller factors. 7 is prime; 8 is composite.

processes: Expressing numbers as products of primes
plainLanguageExplanation: A prime number is a whole number bigger than 1 that has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 7 is prime because only 1 and 7 divide it evenly. 8 is composite because 1, 2, 4, and 8 all divide it. One is not prime (it has just one factor) and not composite. Primes are the 'atoms' of arithmetic: every whole number bigger than 1 can be built by multiplying primes together in one unique way — 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. This is called prime factorization, and it is exactly what makes primes so important.

keyFacts.label: Definition
keyFacts.value: A whole number > 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself

keyFacts.label: Not prime
keyFacts.value: 1 is neither prime nor composite; even numbers > 2 are composite

keyFacts.label: Unique build
keyFacts.value: Every number has ONE unique prime factorization (60 = 2×2×3×5)

whyItMatters: Primes are the building blocks of every whole number. They drive prime factorization, which simplifies fractions, finds least common multiples, and unlocks the cryptography that keeps passwords and online messages secure. Knowing primes helps you see the structure inside numbers.
didYouKnow: There is no largest prime — mathematicians proved the primes go on forever. Today the biggest known primes have millions of digits and power the security of your passwords.
compareReason: Primes are defined by factors (exactly two), so comparing prime vs. factor-count shows how the same idea of factors sorts all numbers into prime or composite.
